course.title: Docker — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first course covering container fundamentals, Docker CLI, images, Dockerfiles, BuildKit/Buildx, storage, networking, Compose, registries, application containerization, debugging, security, observability, CI/CD, production delivery, and optional Swarm specialization. All content remains draft until technical review and lab verification.
course.version_scope: Official Docker documentation checked 2026-10-20. Content is version-adaptive rather than pinned to one release number: verify each installation, CLI flag, Compose feature, builder driver, platform, and output against the installed Docker Engine/Desktop, Compose, and Buildx. BuildKit/Buildx and the Compose Specification are the primary learning path; Docker Swarm is optional.
audience: testers, system administrators, cloud and platform engineers
prerequisites: Basic computer usage; familiarity with files, directories, environment variables, ports, and a terminal is helpful but not mandatory. Use a local Docker installation or approved isolated lab. Cluster, remote daemon, production deployment, and security exercises require appropriate authorization.
learning_outcomes: Explain containerization, image/container differences, the Engine architecture, and container lifecycle.
Install/verify Docker, use the CLI safely, build efficient images, and manage registries and multi-platform outputs.
Design persistent storage, container networks, Compose stacks, and externalized application configuration.
Troubleshoot containerized applications and apply practical security, logging, health, and resource controls.
Automate image tests and releases, deploy and recover services, and document repeatable professional workflows.
